one_liner: Rust async framework for building HTTP proxies; replaced Cloudflare's NGINX-based edge proxy with less CPU, memory and TTFB.
what_it_does: A set of Rust crates (pingora, pingora-core, pingora-proxy, pingora-load-balancing, pingora-cache, ...) for writing your own HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 reverse proxies, load balancers and gateways. You implement the ProxyHttp trait (only upstream_peer() is required) and hook request/response filter phases similar to OpenResty's *_by_lua callbacks; a Server hosts Services, handles YAML config, daemonization and graceful upgrade. It is a library, not a binary: there is no nginx.conf equivalent, so it is not a drop-in replacement.
how_it_is_fast: One multithreaded process on Tokio instead of NGINX's worker processes, so upstream connection pools are shared across all threads; Cloudflare says the TTFB gain comes from this connection reuse, not faster per-request code. The pool keeps a small lock-free hot queue (crossbeam ArrayQueue, 16 slots) per connection group in front of a mutex-protected map. pingora-runtime adds a non-work-stealing multi-thread runtime (N isolated single-threaded Tokio runtimes), and pingora-timeout replaces tokio::time::timeout with lazily-armed timers rounded to 10 ms ticks and shared across timeouts (claimed ~4 ns vs ~107 ns per iteration).
when_to_use: Building a custom reverse proxy, API gateway or load balancer in Rust where routing, retry and header logic must be code rather than config
High-connection-count proxying to many origins where per-worker pools in NGINX give low upstream connection reuse and extra TLS handshakes
Replacing an OpenResty/Lua or C/C++ proxy module with memory-safe code while keeping phase-style request/response hooks
Linux x86_64 or aarch64 deployments that need zero-downtime binary upgrades via listening-socket handoff
gRPC and WebSocket proxying with pluggable TLS backends (OpenSSL, BoringSSL, s2n-tls)
when_not_to_use: You want a configurable server you run without writing Rust: there is no config language, static file serving (issue #40 still open) or module ecosystem comparable to nginx

Short-lived upstream connections or simple pass-through proxying: in one user's 8-core wrk test (issue #372) Pingora matched nginx at ~30K req/s but used ~70% CPU vs ~50%; it only pulled ahead (~50K req/s) with upstream keepalive, at ~80% CPU
You need HTTP/3/QUIC: issue #95 is still open and labeled 'Long Term Goal'
You need a stable API or non-Linux production: pre-1.0 (0.9.0, 2026-09-04) with breaking changes each minor release, caching labeled experimental, macOS best-effort and Windows community-only
Running versions before 0.8.0 on untrusted traffic: two critical request-smuggling CVEs (CVE-2026-2833, CVE-2026-2835) and a cache-poisoning CVE (CVE-2026-2836) were fixed only in 0.8.0

integration.dependencies: tokio, h2, httparse, http, bytes, parking_lot, crossbeam-queue, flate2/brotli/zstd and more; TLS via one feature: openssl (needs Perl), boringssl (needs Clang), s2n, or rustls (experimental)
integration.platforms: Linux x86_64 and aarch64 (tier 1); other Unix incl. macOS best-effort with missing features; Windows preliminary/community-only
integration.thread_safety: Multithreaded by design: each Service owns its own Tokio runtime (work-stealing by default, or N isolated single-threaded runtimes), one task per downstream connection; your ProxyHttp impl and its per-request CTX must be Send + Sync
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — replaces nginx's reverse-proxy role only after you write the proxy logic in Rust; no nginx.conf compatibility, no static file serving or nginx modules

gotchas: Only one TLS feature (openssl, boringssl, s2n, rustls) can be enabled at a time; with none, only plaintext HTTP is available, and rustls is marked highly experimental
Connection reuse is keyed on the full Peer (IP:port, scheme, SNI, client cert, verification and proxy settings); any difference means a separate pool, and idle_timeout 0 disables pooling
Before 0.8.0 the default cache key ignored the Host header (CVE-2026-2836); the default was removed and you must write your own cache key callback
Several users reported memory that grows under load and does not come back (issues #372, #447); a contributor suggested jemalloc, and an empty-PoolNode leak (#748) was fixed only in 0.9.0
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Pingora over H2O or Sogou Workflow when the job is a programmable reverse proxy or load balancer and you want Rust memory safety plus upstream connection pools shared across threads; pick H2O for a configurable HTTP server with static files, or Workflow for a C++ server/client framework with a published QPS benchmark against nginx.
verified_claims_summary: Cloudflare's 2022 blog compares production edge traffic on Pingora with its retired NGINX-based proxy: 5 ms lower median and 80 ms lower p95 TTFB, about 70% less CPU and 67% less memory for the same load, and one customer's upstream connection reuse rising from 87.1% to 99.92% (160x fewer new origin connections). These are unreproducible production aggregates with no hardware, compiler or methodology stated, and the blog attributes the latency gain to cross-thread connection sharing rather than faster code.
status_note: Actively maintained by Cloudflare (0.9.0 released 2026-09-04, last commit 2026-09-11), Apache-2.0 and usable as crates today, but pre-1.0 with frequent breaking changes and a caching layer still labeled alpha/experimental.
